Let’s examine the behavior of sr() as a function of . The reactive cross section sr(), calculated using Equation 18.13, is negative for all values of  , a; these solutions are incompatible with the physical interpretation of the cross section as an area and must be rejected. sr() 5 0 when  5 a and becomes positive when  . a, so we identify a as the threshold energy. sr() is small near the threshold energy, increases with increasing  and finally saturates at sr() 5 sc, the hard sphere cross section, when  becomes much larger than a, as shown in Figure 18.14. We interpret this behavior as follows. The cross section is very small at low energy because the energy delivered along the line of centers is small. The reactive, or effective, cross section, interpreted as an area, increases with increasing  be­ cause more energy is being made available along the line of centers. The reactive cross section saturates at the hard sphere value, which means that every collision leads to reaction.
